We [New Englanders] look upon the states, not as separated, but as united. We love to dwell on that union, and on the mutual happiness which it has so much promoted. . . . In our contemplation, Carolina and Ohio are parts of the same country. . . . We do not impose geographical limits to our patriotic feeling or regard. . . .

—Senator Daniel Webster, reply to Senator Robert Hayne, January 1830

In this reply, Daniel Webster is reacting to —

options.label: A
options.text: the inability of citizens to elect Supreme Court justices

options.label: B
options.text: an attempted nullification of a federal law by a state

options.label: C
options.text: a proposal to revise the amendment process of the U.S. Constitution

options.label: D
options.text: the federal seizure of private land for transportation networks

visual_elements: quotation box containing text from Senator Daniel Webster
